books.section: Topic 4.8 Jackson and Federal Power, A. The Second Two-Party System: The Democrats and the Whigs
The Whig Party and the Second Party System
The Jackson Presidency and Jacksonian Democracy

stimulus.text: The campaign lithograph, published in 1840, shows General William Henry Harrison in military uniform with a sword, under the words 'GENERAL WM. H. HARRISON.' A wreath names his victories: 'Tippecanoe, Fort Meigs and the Thames.' The Whigs campaigned for Harrison with the slogan 'Tippecanoe and Tyler Too' and with log cabins and hard cider as symbols.
stimulus.source_note: Lithograph 'General Wm. H. Harrison of Tippecanoe, Fort Meigs and the Thames,' published 1840 (Library of Congress). Public domain; image viewed before writing.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note
stem: The Whigs' use of log cabins and hard cider in 1840 best shows that the Whigs had

options.text: rejected popular campaigning as undignified and unworthy of gentlemen
options.misconception: The Whigs opposed Jackson, so it is easy to think they opposed everything about his politics, including his style.

options.text: wanted to limit voting to men who owned property
options.misconception: The Whigs were the party of order, so it is easy to think they wanted a narrower electorate.

options.text: learned to campaign to ordinary voters, copying Jacksonian mass politics
run on a platform of abolishing the presidency itself
options.misconception: The Whigs attacked Jackson's strong presidency, so it is easy to think they wanted the office itself gone.

rationales.A: The Whigs embraced rallies, songs, and symbols; they did not reject popular campaigning but copied it.
rationales.B: By 1840 most white men could vote, and the Whigs chased those votes; no Whig platform called for restoring property rules.
rationales.C: Log cabins and hard cider were props for ordinary voters, the mass-campaign style Jackson's Democrats had invented in 1828.
rationales.D: The Whigs wanted the presidency for Harrison, not its abolition; they ran a candidate, not a campaign against the office.
rationales.general:
1. Name the props. Log cabins and hard cider say 'plain folks,' not 'rich gentlemen.'
2. Ask who invented that style. Jackson's Democrats had won in 1828 by campaigning to ordinary voters with rallies and symbols.
Background: the Whigs, founded to oppose Jackson, beat the Democrats in 1840 by fighting them with their own weapons.
Remember: when rivals start to look alike, ask whose style won — the copier tells you who set the fashion.
